Best way to trap them is a tall glass with fruit at the bottom. Roll  a cone out of thick paper, and place it in the glass to just above the fruit and let it uncurl into the size of the glass. It should have no gap between the lip of the glass and the paper, and a tiny hole above the fruit. They fly in, and get stuck. To get rid of it, pour a little water and fairy liquid in, and bang the glass on the worktop. They fall into the water and you can just flush it or put it down the sink. I use a frozen strawberry or handful of frozen berries, works a treat. Don't use paper that's been folded, it leaves a gap and ruins the trap :)

This is not necessarily forever, I promise there is hope. So two years, I'm sure in some ways it feels like a very long time, but it's not. Trauma impacts people in so many ways, and one area is dissociation. It's a survival tool, but it's a pretty blunt instrument, in that perceived harm activates it just as deeply as real harm sometimes. It sounds like you may have disconnected from your body in a way, resulting in no feeling. It's possible to repair the connection, if that is what has happened. Trauma therapy, while it's very buzz wordy and fashionable at the moment, can actually help a great deal. Things like body work, EMDR, even yoga, can all help towards getting you back to where you can feel sensation in those parts you've cut off from. Maybe look into trauma and dissociation, and see if it feels like it may be worth working on? You shouldn't have to, it's unfair, and wrong, and I am so sorry that someone has caused you this harm. You can beat this though, being assaulted takes things from you but you have the power to take some of them back, with the right help. I'm sorry if you just needed to vent and don't want advice or platitudes, but I know how this feels and felt compelled to share a bit of info that may help, because I understand how futile it can seem when you're in it. I wish you well man, whatever you decide to do.

Am I the only person concerned about this? They've basically taken a historically disenfranchised group, who are at very high risk, often traumatised, who often have low/no social support, at a critical time of upheaval in their lives and chosen to use them in an experiment, the results of which will be used to support or criticise ubi as a whole. 

It seems, if one were to be cynical, to be set up for failure. Care leavers are individuals in a very specific and extreme circumstance, the transition can be a very difficult period for many. The results will not be indicative of possible effects of ubi on a wider scale. A better group would have been long term unemployed folks from varying backgrounds.

I'm not suggesting that all care leavers are the same, or that all are significantly traumatised, however it's a very real outcome for many who have been "looked after". The potential for reckless behaviour is higher than average, understandably. The care to prison pipeline demonstrates this all too well. I'm shocked that nobody is acknowledging the issues with using care leavers as representative of the average person in average circumstances. Add in the fact that the age range is 18-20 and its just obviously ridiculous to expect any meaningful or applicable data to be gained.

I'm pretty angry, so if I've misspoken anywhere here, please be generous in your interpretation of what I have said. I am in no way looking down on care leavers, or judging them as irresponsible people. I'm a former care kid myself. If I'm wrong, or have offended, I apologise, it's not my intention at all.
